races.title: State Assembly, District 49
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mike Fong
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented California's 49th Assembly District (San Gabriel Valley) since February 2022. Earlier he served on the Los Angeles Community College District Board of Trustees (2015–2022). His past work includes policy director at the City of Los Angeles Department of Neighborhood Empowerment, deputy mayor and councilman's aide.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and California Young Democrats endorsed him in 2026.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Mike Fong's birthplace or of when his family came to California. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, police funding, gun laws, abortion or school choice. The list of bills he sponsored did not load on the page we read. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or statements on data centers or development. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any recent cycle.

local.label: Roots 90: Wikipedia says he graduated from Francisco Bravo Medical Magnet High School and attended East Los Angeles College, then earned degrees at UCLA and CSU Northridge, and later held Los Angeles-area offices; his birthplace is not stated.

cands.name: Long David Liu
cands.bio: Southern California attorney and business owner who describes himself as a father and published author. He ran as a Republican for California State Assembly District 49 in 2024 and 2026, losing to incumbent Mike Fong both times. No elected office held.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (2024 and 2026) and Reform California (2026), per Ballotpedia.
His campaign site lists endorsements from Michael Antonovich, Michael Gates, Philip Chen, Burton Brink and Daniel Deng.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Long David Liu was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no record of elected office and no details on his law practice or businesses. We found no documented positions on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no news reporting on controversies or foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. The Ballotpedia education entry, a Ph.D. from Whittier Law School, is unclear and could not be checked.
